w: Housed in a 13th-century Dominican convent fused with a 1906 former public bathhouse, this museum holds Matthias Grunewald's Isenheim Altarpiece plus a large collection of local and international art spanning prehistory to today. Roughly 200,000 visitors a year make it Alsace's most-visited museum.
s: Alsace's most-visited museum, in a medieval convent
_facts: Housed in a 13th-century Dominican convent and a 1906 former public baths building
Home to Matthias Grunewald's Isenheim Altarpiece
A Musee de France label; roughly 200,000 visitors a year, the most-visited museum in Alsace

w: Built in the principal Gothic style, this Catholic church is properly a collegiate church -- hence its formal name, the Collegiale Saint-Martin -- but its sheer scale has earned it the local nickname Cathedrale Saint-Martin, even though Colmar has never actually been a bishopric's seat.
s: A Gothic collegiate church locals call the cathedral
_facts: Roman Catholic church in the principal Gothic architectural style
Formally the Collegiale Saint-Martin, a former collegiate church
Locally nicknamed Cathedrale Saint-Martin for its large dimensions, though Colmar was never a bishopric seat

w: Known also as the Koifhus, this Gothic and Renaissance customs house has carried protected-monument status since 1930 and was the birthplace of General Jean Rapp. Once the seat of Colmar's civic and trading life, it now houses a restaurant alongside temporary exhibitions and fairs -- commerce, still, just gentler.
_facts: Also known as the Koifhus; Gothic and Renaissance old customs house
Classified as a monument historique since 1930
Birthplace of General Jean Rapp
Now houses a restaurant plus temporary exhibitions and fairs

w: Raised between 1847 and 1849 on part of the old Unterlinden convent, this circular theatre follows the Italian tradition with three tiered galleries behind a five-bay facade. A 2000 restoration kept it running, and it still draws around 30,000 visitors a year, next door to the Unterlinden Museum.
s: An Italian-style theatre built over an old convent
_facts: Built 1847-1849, replacing part of the old Unterlinden convent
Circular room in the Italian theatre tradition, with three galleries and a five-bay facade
Restored in 2000; roughly 30,000 visitors a year, next to the Unterlinden Museum

w: Sculptor Auguste Bartholdi was born in this house on rue des Marchands, now a museum devoted to his life and work, labeled a Musee de France. Two 17th-century doors were listed as historic monuments in 1926, and the courtyard holds his own statue, the Grands Soutiens du Monde.
s: Sculptor Auguste Bartholdi's own birthplace museum
_facts: Museum at 30 rue des Marchands, sculptor Auguste Bartholdi's birthplace
Musee de France label; Maison des Illustres label since 2011
Two 17th-century doors registered as monuments historiques in 1926
Courtyard holds Bartholdi's statue Les Grands Soutiens du Monde

w: Opened in 1864, this 23-kilometre canal -- a branch of the wider Rhone-Rhine Canal -- climbs through three locks to link Colmar directly to the river Rhine at Biesheim. A quiet feat of 19th-century engineering, threading water through the flat Alsace countryside toward the border.
s: The 19th-century canal linking Colmar to the Rhine
_facts: Colmar branch of the Rhone-Rhine Canal, connecting Colmar to the Rhine at Biesheim
23 km long with three locks
Inaugurated 13 November 1864
